excludedFindingFamilies: PUB86-ROOT-* and later publisher-successor findings remain in the separate publisher successor record and are not part of these 150 IDs.

findings.statement: Catalog-v2 disagreed with the still-v1 registry.
Catalog-v2 allowed a free-text exact-definition exemption without governed proof.
Catalog-v2 assigned the exemption at source-node rather than source-node, operand and data-family support-edge granularity.
Catalog-v2 did not enforce empirical independence, exact-definition provenance and currency as separate conjunctive requirements.
Catalog-v2 lacked exact successor provenance.
Catalog-v2 left SRC-ADR0036 role and membership ambiguous.
mandatory review invoked a verifier mode forbidden by the verifier's closed mode set.
negative controls lacked frozen IDs, mutations, witnesses and detectors.
review runs were self-attested and their generated logs were not tracked.
review closure omitted load-bearing dependencies and allowed a shared semantic-reducer attack.
successor review could omit earlier rejected findings.
heterogeneous publication-review rows had no deterministic total order.
ignored recovery scratch under `evidence/` conflicted with the tracked evidence boundary and integrity test.
the bespoke publisher/review/recovery stack duplicated the shared evidence seam without a justified new attack surface.
contributor/model disjointness was free-text and its attestation limit understated.
the active plan still carried stale “not integrated” prose.
durable publication lacked an explicit commit, clean-checkout verify and exact `npm test` boundary.
assessment `schedulingWitnesses` was mandatory but undefined.
both `entryEvidence.kind` discriminators lacked permitted literals.
citation evidence could support load-bearing claims without adequate review.
source-review provenance could not establish reviewer kind, context or disjointness.
the positive/nonzero decimal grammar could not encode ordinary negative or zero Celsius inputs and left conversions unstated.
pressure output conversion and uncertainty were author-selected rather than independently recomputable.
the independence edge universe contradicted the arm-specific catalog arrays.
an independence edge could pass with empty claim/segment evidence.
currency alternated between effective heads and every historical descriptor.
entry-specific scheduling used stale occurrence screen state.
source inputs omitted manual page-source bytes and had ambiguous path roots.
“active catalog source-node” had two incompatible derivations.
reviewer-assignment rows lacked the key required by heterogeneous ordering.
checkpoint review ordering was incomplete and contributor/provenance equality was contradictory.
`reviewedAssessmentRevisionIds` named a descriptor hash that did not exist.
mandatory reexecution was self-attested and required an impossible verifier mode.
the required review set omitted CLI, transitive code and other load-bearing bytes.
preparation/publication artifact sets, roots and verifier inputs were underdetermined.
entry wording referenced a stale independence field.
null-byte authoritative external nodes had no explicit fail-closed treatment.
media-type inventory mapping and tool/version were not frozen.
alias-history prose conflicted with final-state-only derivation.
the location and immutability of the eventual 0/0 review record were unclear.
a fabricated or wrongly converted pressure output row could pass without source-segment, transcription, unit, solver-mapping or governed-repeat binding.
TAX2 said `REGISTERED` inside a globally unregistered candidate.
hard kills can orphan shared-publisher staging or leave a renamed bundle before `evidence/MANIFEST.json`; recovery authority was undefined.
the 20 symbolic fixtures and alternative-worded mutations were not exact, governed bytes.
the attacked verifier also executed and witnessed its mutations, violating independent negative-control proof.
published-byte rederivation was impossible without the ignored raw/source/ extraction bytes.
review payload schemas, ordering, required commands, logs and check-to- evidence mapping were underdetermined.
the 36 inherited findings existed only in mutable plan prose, not a governed machine registry bound into semantic closure.
contributor IDs hashed mutable/free-text attestations, allowing one session to appear disjoint by changing wording.
the transitive import-resolution algorithm and permitted shared exports were not frozen.
the durable post-commit clean-checkout result, tested commit, logs and acceptance verdict had no named record.
request identities, initial ordinals and response-driven pagination DAG were not uniquely constructible.
citation and Rule 12 expansion omitted exact truncation, query/author and partial-date rules.
attempt/result/retry/crash schemas and concurrent reservation authority were incomplete and race-prone.
provider projections/rank, screening normalization, identifier reduction and the opaque route contract were not reproducible.
assessment/source/inventory/segment/relation/edge payloads remained prose-only; `assessmentId` was self-referential.
the claimed clean-checkout semantic rederivation required ignored response, source and extraction bytes that the checkout did not contain.
matched-pressure admission failed to require air, positive supersaturation, supported temperatures or a computable match/confound operator.
controls, fixtures, review checks, prior findings and import closure could execute vacuously or could not be reconstructed.
final payload schemas/order and shared-publisher wrapper inputs were not frozen.
the no-scratch crash claim contradicted the shared publisher's possible orphaned staging directory.
active plans quoted charter v1.19 after charter v1.20 was accepted.
the stated unresolved source-node set omitted BIPM/CGPM no-local-byte nodes.
the immutable location/format of the eventual acceptance record was unnamed.
backward/forward citation roots, qualifying roots and recursively expanded relation members were undefined, so conforming executors could search different graphs.
correction/version/same-author Rule 12 construction, authors, dates and derived pagination were underdetermined.
pressure values need not be distinct and load-bearing conditions could differ as unspecified “pressure-specific measured inputs,” admitting confounded comparisons.
pressure screening did not require a number and omitted common `Pa`, `kPa`, `Torr` and `mmHg` forms, creating systematic false-negative exclusions.

transverse-span mappings used `latticeExtents.tExtent`, a rotation-dependent trigger span rather than an objective Cartesian physical observable; the existing aspect-ratio denominator also changed under the reviewer's explicit 60-degree witness.
all three arms also referenced BIPM/CGPM no-local-byte nodes, so the current unresolved-set prose was incomplete or the exact-definition policy needed correction.
source decimal handling omitted common printed and scientific-notation forms or a traceable normalized-transcription field.
the register's exact bytes were not stable under a clean Windows checkout; with `core.autocrlf=true`, the reviewed LF bytes would become a different registered object.
the global 243-stage claim contradicted the entry-specific 108/135 route- query roots and therefore could not drive one deterministic schedule.
recovery after a real process kill or a crash between bundle rename and manifest finalization had no authoritative, non-destructive reducer.
the acceptance-review verdict was not machine-closed over required checks, logs, prior findings, and the exact reviewed closure.
the final shared-publisher call, option set, schemas, fixtures, transitive imports, semantic independence, and future-behavior boundary remained underdefined.

Section 11's statement that no reviewer had parsed the registry became false as soon as review occurred; reviewer observations belong in an append-only external review record rather than the frozen scientific protocol.
the exact JSON schemas remained undefined and `assessmentId` depended on the object that was supposed to contain it.
the global page schedule contradicted the entry-specific route/page counts.
citation and Rule 12 expansion remained unbounded or non-unique.
the immutable attempt state machine omitted reachable reservation, partial, retry, interruption, terminal, and concurrent-writer transitions.
assessment revision and source-replacement rules could leave stale accepted heads or ambiguous authority.
the reduction from attempts and assessments to success, unresolved, or definitive failure was not defined.
independence could pass with a nonempty but scientifically vacuous edge set; it did not require coverage of the candidate and every active operand data family/source node.
pressure transcription, conversion, covariance, uncertainty, and solver-output bindings remained underdetermined.
review-result schemas, required commands, finding closure, and evidence mapping were not exact.
registered controls were symbolic enough to execute vacuously or described mutations that the named witness could not independently prove.
shared-publisher options, staging topology, recovery authority, and the clean- checkout boundary remained underdefined.
the hash-registered prose register was not `-text`, while the catalog's `generatedFrom` hash domain did not say raw, LF-normalized, filtered, or Git-blob bytes.
the validator's claim that it checked all source hashes exceeded the set of source bytes it actually reopened.
closure prose omitted the BIPM/CGPM authoritative nodes that the governed operand catalog named.
a historical eligibility cutoff was used as if it were an actual freeze-time source-currency observation; no final `currencyAsOfUtc` was bound.
243 route/query combinations were mislabeled as page requests; the frozen initial-page schedule was not uniquely derived and had no exact root/seed set.

source conditions were not bound to the LK solver's supported temperature, positive maintained supersaturation, pressure, duration, and checkpoint/output domain; current `grow-lk` also has no pressure argument and defaults to 101325 Pa.
proposed output mappings were not objective, physically comparable observables; lattice trigger span, projection/fill definitions, and the comparison endpoint remained unfrozen.
uncertainty pairing, covariance, repeated-measurement reduction, and contrast propagation were insufficient to define a quantitative pressure comparison.
source language, translation/OCR competence, tool identity, and human-review adequacy should be machine-checkable where they support a load-bearing claim.
SOURCE-GRAPH-CLOSURE ? a single acquired source need not equal its sole inventory member, and rationale segment IDs need not exist in the reviewed-segment universe.
ZERO-BYTE-REVIEW ? zero-byte extraction and translation records can support adequate evidence.
LANGUAGE-ROLE-SEPARATION ? a translation reviewer may be the original extractor.
EXACT-DECIMAL-GRAMMAR ? `+1e0`, `-0`, and `.5` pass despite the registered decimal grammar and negative-zero ban.
SOURCE-ONLY-STATE-SPACE ? honest zero-row search/access/cap outcomes are impossible, while exact positive `source-compatible-bridge-required` is unrepresentable.
PRESSURE-EVIDENCE-CLOSURE ? unknown pairing/uncertainty evidence and ghost observation IDs pass without forward and reverse referential closure.

PRESSURE-CONTRACT-UNDERDETERMINED ? gas-composition evidence, supersaturation-definition identity, pairing design/population/repeat identity, covariance type/coverage, and honest missing-uncertainty states are not representable.
DEFINITIVE-FAIL-RESURRECTION ? an assessment revision can retract the only definitive solver-compatibility trigger without a reviewed successor.

INDEPENDENCE-FALSE-POSITIVE ? caller-supplied row lists can declare independence while every required edge points to known-missing local bytes; the module also invents an evidence-class field absent from catalog v1.

REVIEW-CLOSURE-VACUITY-AND-ORDER ? empty required/check/run/control/finding universes and reversed arrays pass; command, reviewer provenance/competence, and evidence-log closure are not independently derived.
REDIRECT-VALIDITY ? redirect cycles and non-HTTP(S) `opaque:` targets pass.
UNSTABLE-CANDIDATE-IDENTITY ? neither candidate file is `-text`; a clean `core.autocrlf=true` checkout changes both registered raw SHA-256 identities.
